name: Bulo Stieng
confidence_why: 5 independent first-hand sources agree (4 agree, 0 refine), none contradicts

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Coding '01' fixed-dominant (final/main-syllable stress in disyllabic = sesquisyllabic words, presyllable never stressed) is confirmed by every source opened: Miller 1976:5 (the deciding sketch, quote verified verbatim at the stated locator in the file downloaded now), Haupers 1969:132 (primary phonology, explicitly Bulo dialect), Bon 2010:24 and Bon 2014:83-84 fn.136 (reference grammar of Bulo-group Cambodian Stieng). No contradiction anywhere; languoid identity checks out (Miller's texts 'Bu-Lo Stieng', Haupers 'Bulo dialect', Bon places Cambodian Stieng in the Bulo group). The record is 'adequate' rather than 'well-sourced' only because it rests on a second-hand 1976 syntax sketch with empty top-level quote/cite/grade fields; action: add Haupers 1969:132 and Bon 2014:84 fn.136 as co-deciding citations and set an strength of the evidence. no reclassification.

sources.citation: Miller 1976, An overview of Stieng grammar, SIL-UND Work Papers 20:7, sec 1.2.1 Word Pattern p.5 (PDF via the Internet Archive of commons.und.edu article 1218)
sources.quote: Stieng words may be either monosyllabic (eg. poh 'village') or disyllabic (eg. parhey 'red'). Disyllabic words are stressed on the final (main) syllable. The initial (pre-syllable) is never stressed. [scanned normalized: 'Dioyllabic word[~ are stre~rned on the final (main) syllable']

sources.citation: Bon, Noëllie. 2014. Une grammaire de la langue stieng, langue en danger du Cambodge et du Vietnam. Thèse de doctorat, Université Lumière Lyon 2 (HAL tel-03025620). 645 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: Sesquisyllabe = 'une syllabe non accentuée avec un noyau non phonémique (dite mineure ou faible) ainsi que d'une syllabe majeure (ou principale)'; fn.136: 'Un mot sesquisyllabique est réalisé avec la dynamique suivante : la syllabe faible est non accentuée et brève tandis que la syllabe principale est réalisée plus longue, avec une accentuation forte et légèrement montante.' Word canon (C(C)(v)(C)).C(C)V(C); 25% of Bon09 lexicon sesquisyllabic, 75% monosyllabic.
sources.locator: Partie II ch.1 'Système phonologique de BS', sec 1.1.1 Structure du mot, printed pp.83-84 (PDF pp.100-101), incl. footnote 136; p.22 places Cambodian Stieng in the Bulo group
sources.note: Only full reference grammar (645 pp) with a phonology chapter; confirms unstressed minor + stressed major syllable (pp.83-84, fn.136); our classification rested on a 1976 64-pp syntax sketch.

sources.citation: Bon, Noëllie. 2010. Phonology of the Stieng language: a rime study. Journal of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 3.2:22-48 (HAL hal-03025567).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: simple words can be monosyllabic or sesquisyllabic ... one weak syllable, which is light, with a non-phonemic vowel, and one main syllable which is heavy, with a phonemic vowel - with the stress falling on the main syllable.
sources.locator: p.24 (PDF p.4), sec 2.1 Word and syllabic canon
sources.note: Modern phonology article; p.24 states stress falls on the main syllable of sesquisyllables.

sources.quote: Words then may be monosyllabic ... or disyllabic (/bonad/ '24-hr period'). Disyllabic words are stressed on the main (second) syllable.
sources.locator: p.132, sec 1 'Syllable and word structure' (image-only PDF; scanned text); p.131 states 'This study represents the Bulo dialect.. in Phuoc Long'
sources.note: Primary phonology of exactly the Bulo dialect by the field linguist whose data Miller 1976 summarizes; states final (main-syllable) stress on p.132 — should replace/join Miller as the deciding cite.
